chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I do not love anything from your world except women and perfume.'

key_terms.الدنيا: The temporal world, as opposed to the hereafter (al-akhira); here used to mean worldly pleasures and possessions
key_terms.الطيب: Perfume, fragrance, or pleasant scent; also used in broader sense as all things pleasant and pure
key_terms.النساء: Women; in this context referring to the Prophet's wives or women in general in the context of lawful marriage

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad love from the world?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) expressed his affections within this world, stating his love for women and fragrant perfume. This prophetic statement comes from the 'Book of Marriage' in al-Kafi and reflects the Islamic tradition of honoring the Prophet's human nature and legitimate expressions of love. The original audience — Shia scholars and students — would have understood this as affirming the sanctity of marriage and sensory pleasures within permissible Islamic bounds, while the Prophet's zuhd (detachment) from worldly gain remained intact.
